claims.claim: Didymus the Blind (c. 313–398) was a Christian theologian in the Church of Alexandria, where he taught for about half a century.
Didymus the Blind was a student of Origen.
Didymus became head of the Alexandrian catechetical school, appointed by Athanasius.
Didymus remained a layman all his life.
In 553 the Second Council of Constantinople condemned Didymus's works, along with those of Origen and Evagrius Ponticus, but not his person.
Because of this condemnation, most of Didymus's works were not copied during the European Middle Ages and thus were lost.
A 1531 edition of In omnes epistolas Canonicas brevis enarratio was published in Cologne, combined with Didymus's De spiritu sancto in Jerome's Latin translation.
Manuscripts of In Epistulas Catholicas Breuis Enarratio survive in the Biblioteca Vallicelliana in Rome (MS F 9) and the Monasterio de El Escorial (MS Υ II 1).
